cf.title: pg_upgrade: Prevent premature startup of the new cluster

input.subject: Prevent premature startup of pg_upgrade targets

verdict_reasoning: No surviving objection challenges the problem or the goal: message #3 reproduces the unprotected window and message #2 agrees in principle. The one surviving objection, replication-ondisk-2, is a fixable design point about the rsync standby case, which v1 defers and does not make worse. What remains is a decision for a committer who knows pg_upgrade and server start, because the patch adds a new refusal at startup. Confidence is medium because the thread is short and nobody has reviewed v1.

brief.title: pg_upgrade: refuse normal startup of the new cluster during upgrade
brief.problem: pg_upgrade checks only at the start that the new cluster is not running, so an external start during file transfer, pg_resetwal or the final sync goes undetected. Such a server can write WAL and consume xids and MultiXacts while pg_upgrade still reports success. This affects operators whose automation or tooling may start the target cluster too early.
brief.proposed_design: pg_upgrade creates an fsynced marker file in the new data directory before it first modifies the cluster and removes it, again fsynced, after the last step that starts the new cluster. checkDataDir() refuses to start the server while the file exists unless binary-upgrade mode (-b) is set, which pg_upgrade uses for its own starts. A failed or interrupted upgrade leaves the file in place.
user_visible_surface: New file pg_upgrade_in_progress in the new cluster's data directory during and after a failed upgrade.
New FATAL error "data directory ... is being upgraded by pg_upgrade" with DETAIL and HINT at server start, also in single-user mode.
New macro for the file name in access/xlog_internal.h, next to XLOG_CONTROL_FILE, usable from frontend code.
New paragraph in the pg_upgrade documentation describing the marker and the need to re-run initdb after a failure.
author_claims: A production copy-mode upgrade completed successfully, then showed corruption weeks later, with evidence the target was started during the upgrade; causation is not proven.
Shubhra reproduced a 16 to 17 copy-mode upgrade where an externally created table survived into the upgraded cluster.
With the patch, that reproduction fails with the new error and the upgrade then completes normally.
check-world passes, including all transfer modes in 006_transfer_modes.pl, and --check never creates the marker.
Daniel Gustafsson called the idea reasonable as an extra layer of protection.
brief.thread_state: Nik proposed the idea, Daniel Gustafsson agreed in principle, and Shubhra posted v1, which CFbot reports needs a rebase. Nobody has replied to v1 or to its open points on the file name, fsync under --no-sync and the rsync/standby case.
unclear: The patch does not handle standby upgrades with rsync, where the marker may need to stay after pg_upgrade completes.
The material does not say how a user who knows the risk can override the marker, other than deleting the file by hand.
The material does not say whether tools that read the data directory, such as pg_resetwal, pg_rewind or pg_checksums, respect the marker.
The material does not say whether forcing initdb after any failure is stricter than today's documented recovery steps for each transfer mode.
The material does not say whether placing the macro in xlog_internal.h is the right header for a non-WAL file name.

prior_attempts.title: Set default transactions to read-only at servers start in pg_upgrade
prior_attempts.reason: The visible messages do not show why. The last messages, from August 2021, still debate where to block background workers: in bgworker_should_start_now(), in RegisterBackgroundWorker(), or not in the backend at all. They also ask whether extensions could fail when their workers do not run. No message explains the withdrawal in December 2021.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P7 limited writes by the servers that pg_upgrade itself starts. This proposal refuses servers that someone else starts while pg_upgrade works, so the P7 debate about where to block background workers does not apply.

prior_attempts.title: Do not start bgworker processes during binary upgrade
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P14 kept background workers from starting in binary-upgrade mode. This proposal leaves binary-upgrade servers alone and refuses normal starts while the marker exists.

prior_attempts.title: pg_upgrade allows itself to be run twice (initdb)
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P24 dealt with pg_upgrade running twice against the same new cluster. This proposal blocks server start after a failed run but does not say whether pg_upgrade refuses a new cluster that already has the marker.

prior_attempts.title: Improve documentation for pg_upgrade, standbys and rsync
prior_attempts.quote: To be more explicit though- we should write a tool to do this. We shouldn't try to document a way to do it because it's hard to get right.
prior_attempts.reason: Stephen Frost argued that this procedure is too hard to get right in an rsync command or a documented procedure, and that a tool should replace it. He proposed moving the text out of the documentation to a wiki. Robert Haas found the new order of the preparation steps confusing. The author saw no agreement and withdrew the patch.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P6 rewrote the documented rsync procedure for standbys. v1 leaves the rsync case out, so P6's objection would apply only to a follow-up that adds a manual marker removal step.

objections.title: Marker does not cover the documented rsync standby upgrade
objections.failure_scenario: An operator upgrades a primary and then runs the documented rsync to its standbys. Automation starts the new primary after pg_upgrade exits but before rsync finishes, because the marker is already gone. The standby ends up with files that do not match the primary, and the mismatch surfaces only after failover.
objections.argument: Message #1 named this case as one where the marker must outlive pg_upgrade. Message #4 defers it, so v1 protects only the single-node path. A later keep-marker option would need a supported way to remove the marker on the primary and on each rsynced standby. Today the only way is a manual file delete, which adds one more step to a procedure that [P6] records as hard to get right by hand.
objections.author_must_show: How would the marker design extend to the rsync standby procedure, and by what supported command would an operator remove it on the primary and the standbys?

precedents.title: Improve documentation for pg_upgrade, standbys and rsync

critic.reasoning: Message #1 names the rsync case as needing the marker to outlive pg_upgrade, and message #4 defers it without saying how an operator would remove the marker. The scenario exists today and v1 does not worsen it, so it is a design question for the author and stays fixable.

refuted.title: Marker removal point may fall before the final data directory sync
refuted.failure_scenario: pg_upgrade removes the marker after its last server start, then begins the final sync, and the host loses power before the sync finishes. On reboot the marker is gone, so automation starts a cluster whose transferred files were never made durable. Nobody learns of it until corruption shows up later.
refuted.argument: The commit message lists the final sync as one of the unprotected windows. Message #3 promised removal "only after the final sync", but message #4 says the marker goes away "after the last step that starts the new cluster". In pg_upgrade the data directory sync runs after the last server start. Removal must be ordered after that sync, and the ordering must still hold under --no-sync, or the durability guarantee the marker implies does not cover the case it names.
refuted.author_must_show: Is the marker unlinked and its directory fsynced only after the final data directory sync completes, and what does the design guarantee under --no-sync?

critic.reasoning: In pg_upgrade's main(), the data directory sync (initdb --sync-only) runs before issue_warnings_and_set_wal_level(), which is the last step that starts the new cluster. Removal "after the last step that starts the new cluster" is therefore already after the final sync.

refuted.title: Protected window depends on call placement that nothing enforces
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a step to pg_upgrade that writes to the new cluster after the marker is removed. An operator's automation starts the target during that step. The upgrade still reports success, and nothing in the build or tests flags that the step is unprotected.
refuted.argument: The marker protects only what runs between its creation and its removal in pg_upgrade.c, and future pg_upgrade steps must be placed with that in mind. The material does not agree on where removal happens. Message #3 says after the final sync, while message #4 says after the last step that starts the new cluster, and message #1 names syncing as one of the unprotected phases. The tests in message #4 check that the marker exists and is removed, but not that every modifying step runs while it exists.
refuted.author_must_show: Does the marker cover the final data directory sync, and how would a test or assertion catch a future step that modifies the new cluster after removal?

critic.reasoning: The scenario needs a hypothetical future patch that adds a modifying step after the last server start, where only the completion banner runs today. The claim that the final sync is uncovered is wrong, because that sync runs before the last server start.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: pg_upgrade creates and removes a new file, pg_upgrade_in_progress, in the new cluster's data directory.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: Message #1 says the rsync standby procedure may need the marker to stay after pg_upgrade; v1 defers this.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: checkDataDir() gains a permanent startup check, and pg_upgrade must keep marker creation and removal correctly placed.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How would the marker extend to the rsync standby procedure, and which supported command would remove it on the primary and on each standby?
After a failed upgrade, is deleting pg_upgrade_in_progress by hand a supported way to start the new cluster, or is initdb the only supported path?
Is the rule to re-run initdb after any failure stricter than today's documented recovery steps for each transfer mode?
Does pg_upgrade refuse a new cluster that already has the marker, and do pg_resetwal, pg_rewind and pg_checksums respect it?
Under --no-sync, does pg_upgrade still fsync the creation and the removal of the marker?

committability.owner_note: Daniel Gustafsson agreed in principle in message #2, before any patch existed; nobody has reviewed v1. The owner needs to know pg_upgrade's step order and the server start path.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a permanent refusal in checkDataDir(): any case where the marker wrongly stays, or wrongly goes away, becomes a cluster that will not start or an unprotected upgrade.
committability.author_follow_up: Shubhra took the work as a first patch and posted v1 with open points listed; CFbot has reported a needed rebase since 2026-10-16, with no reply yet.

priority.reason: The patch is about 11 KiB over five files and guards pg_upgrade users against a reproduced path to silent corruption (message #3). It needs a rebase and an answer on the rsync standby case before review.

provisional_note: Without the code, the review could not confirm that the marker is created before the first change to the new cluster, or that every server start by pg_upgrade passes -b. It also could not check the fsync behaviour under --no-sync.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Support for upgrading to checksums enabled
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets pg_upgrade run between clusters with different data checksum settings by rewriting page checksums while it copies files. The first version did this automatically in --copy mode, and a later version added an explicit --update-checksums option.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author closed the entry because reviewers showed little interest in the feature or in solving its remaining problems. One problem was still open: copyFile() has a separate Windows code path, and the author did not know how checksum rewriting should work there. He said the feature could not move ahead without an answer to it.

I'm not sensing much enthusiasm for this feature or for working out the
remaining problems, so I'm closing this commitfest entry.

precedents_retrieved.title: add timing information to pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds the elapsed time of each pg_upgrade step to the status output, for example "ok (took 82 ms)", formatted like psql's PrintTiming(). The goal was to show where upgrade time goes and to measure future work on reducing pg_upgrade downtime.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut questioned who besides developers would use the timings and said pg_upgrade output already has too much information that users cannot act on. He suggested that shell tools such as "pg_upgrade | ts" or "ts -i" are enough, and the author agreed to leave it at that unless someone saw a reason to build it in. Only a related fix that raised MESSAGE_WIDTH to 62 was committed.

precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
If it's just for developers and expert users, perhaps existing
shell-level functionality like "pg_upgrade | ts" would suffice?

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade documentation improvement
precedents_retrieved.summary: A documentation patch for pg_upgrade explained what "compatible initdb flags" means for the new cluster: the same encoding, locale and checksum settings as the old one. It told users to find the encoding and locale of template0 with psql -l and the checksum setting with pg_controldata.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut said the cluster locale is better taken from pg_controldata and doubted that pg_upgrade needs the encoding to match. The author asked whether to change the patch to use pg_controldata only, but no revised patch followed. Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback because the thread had died.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade version and path checking
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch set makes pg_upgrade check every executable it uses, require the new binaries to match pg_upgrade's exact major and minor version, and default --new-bindir to pg_upgrade's own directory. It came from Tom Lane's report that pg_upgrade 11.3 would use pg_dump 11.1.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Peter Eisentraut committed 0002 to 0004, which add the executable checks, the --new-bindir default and a typo fix. He found that 0001 compares pg_upgrade's version only with pg_ctl's, so it does not make all binaries match, and proposed a version check for each validate_exec() call instead. On 2019-09-02 the author said a new version would come that week, but no later version appears in the visible messages.
matched_queries: pg_upgrade corruption cluster started during upgrade
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: It compares (new_cluster.bin_version != PG_VERSION_NUM), but new_cluster.bin_version is actually just the version of pg_ctl, so this is just comparing the version of pg_upgrade with the version of pg_ctl, which is not wrong, but doesn't really achieve the full goal of having all binaries match.

precedents_retrieved.title: Backport perl tests for pg_upgrade
precedents_retrieved.summary: Backport the Perl TAP version of the pg_upgrade tests (commit 322becb60) and related follow-up commits to REL_13_STABLE and REL_14_STABLE, replacing test.sh there. precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade: Pass -j option down to vacuumdb
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Peter Eisentraut, Michael Paquier, Tom Lane
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pg_upgrade pass its -j option to the vacuumdb commands in the generated analyze_new_cluster.sh script, so the post-upgrade analyze runs in parallel. Later versions added a VACUUM_OPTS variable to the script and a suggested vacuumdb --jobs command.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Reviewers held that pg_upgrade -j and vacuumdb -j are bound by different resources, so the same value should not be reused, and the generated script is meant to analyze gently. Tom Lane and Michael Paquier did not see most of the patch as better than the status quo and preferred a printed hint or a documentation-only change. The thread then moved to copying statistics in pg_upgrade instead.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Add redo LSN to pgstats files"
Reverted commit(s): Add redo LSN to pgstats files
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit b860848232aa, that was added as a prerequisite for
the support of pgstats data flush across checkpoints, linking a pgstats
file to a specific checkpoint redo LSN.

As reported, this is proving to be currently problematic when going
through a pg_upgrade, that does direct manipulations of the control file
in the new cluster.  The LSN stored in the pgstats file is not able to
cope with any changes done in the control file by pg_upgrade yet,
causing the pgstats file to be discarded when starting the new cluster
after overriding its redo LSN (one is a `pg_resetwal -l` where the new
cluster's start LSN is bumped by a hardcoded value of 8 segments, see
copy_xact_xlog_xid).

The least painful path going forward is likely going to be a refactor of
the pgstats code so as it is possible to read and write some of its data
with some routines in src/common/, so as pg_upgrade or pg_resetwal are
able to update its data.  The main point is that we are going to need a
LSN in the stats file should we make it written at checkpoint time and
not only as part of a shutdown sequence.  It is too late to dive into
these details for v18, so let's revert the change, and let's try to
figure out all the details in the next release cycle.  The pgstats file
is currently only written as part of a shutdown sequence, and its
contents are still lost on crash, same as older releases.

Bump PGSTAT_FILE_FORMAT_ID.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_upgrade allows itself to be run twice (initdb)
precedents_retrieved.summary:
pg_upgrade allows itself to be run twice (initdb)
Threads: pg_upgrade allows itself to be run twice

roaster_notes.note: No recorded rejection reason in the precedents applies to v1. P7 and P14 blocked writes from pg_upgrade's own servers, and P6's objection to hand-run rsync steps would apply only to the deferred standby follow-up, which v1 does not include.

From the standards and compatibility angle the proposal adds no SQL syntax, no GUC, no catalog object and nothing for pg_dump or psql. A successful upgrade leaves no file behind, so existing scripts and the documented standby rsync procedure behave as today. The one new behaviour is that a failed upgrade's new cluster refuses to start, and the documentation already tells users to re-run initdb in that case. The commit message and message #4 differ on whether the marker is removed before or after the final sync; this is a safety question for another angle. The xlog_internal.h placement and the file name are internal and open, as message #4 says.

The proposal adds no WAL records, catalog entries, wire protocol messages or ABI changes. The marker is a transient file that exists only while pg_upgrade runs, so the persistent-state concerns are limited to the two objections above.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. Only the OS user that owns the data directory can create or remove the marker, or start the server with -b. A SQL role with pg_write_server_files could create the file to block a restart, but that role can already overwrite postgresql.auto.conf, so no new path opens.

From the maintenance angle the design is small and general, and it cannot live in an extension. The startup cost is one file check at server start. Only the placement concern above holds. Committability: Daniel Gustafsson agreed only in principle, and no committer has reviewed v1.

No existing feature covers this. Renaming pg_control, as disable_old_cluster() does, would break pg_upgrade's own -b starts and pg_resetwal on the new cluster, and postmaster.pid only guards a running server. An extension cannot act before checkDataDir(), and operator measures such as masking service units do not protect against the automation errors the proposal targets.

The demand angle finds no objection. The patch guards every pg_upgrade user against a reproduced corruption path (message #3), backed by one production case and agreement from a committer (message #2). Its cost is a file check at startup, and only users of a failed upgrade see the stricter initdb rule.
